decisions.reason: As the umbrella dietary-supplement line, it carries visible branding, multiple variants, and fits the announced portfolio-broadening strategy, so sunk investment and public commitment favor persistence.

This skin-and-hair supplement is a smaller and crowded niche product, but it was launched publicly through pharmacies and still sits within the firm's consumer-health expansion, which encourages management to continue it.
The joint-health supplement was given increasing website support after launch and matches a pharmacy-oriented consumer-health logic, making management likely to justify and maintain the investment.

The immune supplement was presented as an innovative addition to the Trivital line, so its visibility and linkage to the broader range make continued commitment likely, especially if weaker sales can be blamed on temporary market conditions.

The generic blood-pressure product had a launch-period problem, but management can frame this as a temporary quality or supplier issue and, given the regulatory and manufacturing investment already made, is still somewhat more likely to persist than exit.

The OTC migraine triptan extends the portfolio into a strategically relevant consumer-health category, and the launch effort and approval-related investment make management inclined to keep it on the market.
